en: PAGASA names tropical cyclones entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility, like Typhoon Odette which heavily damaged Siargao Island in 2021.
The Philippines experiences a wet season from June to November and a dry season from December to May due to shifting monsoon winds.
The rich volcanic soil around Mount Mayon in Albay makes the region highly productive for growing abaca plants used in making ropes.
The Philippines is a top global producer of nickel, an important metal mined from laterite rocks in places like Surigao.
Rainwater seeps into the porous limestone of the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River, creating one of the longest navigable underground rivers globally.
Because the Philippines is located near the equator, it receives direct sunlight year-round, preventing the extreme cold winters seen in distant countries.
Filipino farmers traditionally look for the Balatik constellation, part of Ursa Major, to know when to plant their rice crops.
The gravitational pull of the moon causes high tides in Manila Bay, which local fishermen use to navigate their small bangka boats.
The Valley Fault System stretches across Luzon, meaning cities like Marikina must enforce strict building codes to survive strong earthquakes.
Taal Volcano in Batangas sits inside a lake and erupts explosive steam blasts when hot magma directly touches the cold water.
The amihan or northeast monsoon brings cool, dry air to the Philippines between November and February, making it perfect for drying fish.
White sand beaches in Boracay are made mostly of coral fragments and shells broken down by ocean waves over thousands of years.
